edge.title: The parcel you never sent
edge.anchor: Inshorts reports Bengaluru's unpaid traffic fines have crossed ₹2,048 crore, the kind of real backlog that fake challan links borrow credibility from.
edge.setup: A call or SMS: a courier in your name is held — contraband, expired documents, a customs duty unpaid. There's a small fee to release it, or a case will be filed. Sometimes the caller knows your address, because it leaked from a delivery app.
edge.tell: An unexpected problem whose solution is a small immediate payment to a stranger.
move: No courier or customs process is ever resolved by phone to a UPI ID. Hang up.
If you genuinely expect a parcel, check the tracking number on the courier's own website — never via a link sent to you.
Report at cybercrime.gov.in; don't engage to 'find out more'.
edge.why: Small-fee scams work on expected value: ₹1,500 is below your threshold for serious scrutiny but above zero, and sent at scale. Noticing the shape — unexpected problem, immediate small payment, stranger's account — immunises you against the whole family at once.
edge.variants: Same shape: fake traffic-challan links, electricity bill disconnection SMS, 'your KYC will lapse' payments.

lens.name: Induced demand
lens.one_line: Adding road capacity creates new trips that fill it, so congestion returns at a higher throughput.
lens.detail: People who had given up on a route — shifted their timing, taken transit, moved closer — return once it gets easier. The new lane doesn't serve the old traffic; it reveals suppressed demand that was always there. Measured honestly, travel time often lands back where it started within a few years, now with more vehicles.
elsewhere: Build more parking and more people drive in.
Add engineers to a late project and the scope expands to absorb them.
Widen a hospital's OPD and the waiting room refills.
lens.test: When someone promises more capacity will fix congestion, ask: what was suppressed, and what happens when it comes back?
lens.today: BMRCL has proposed a 10km double-decker structure on the Orange Line to ease bottlenecks at Sarakki, Kamakya and Kadabagere, and a 4km one on Magadi Road. Induced demand says to ask what is suppressed on those roads today: people who leave at odd hours, avoid the corridor or skip the trip. If it gets easier, they return, so judge the project by how many more people it moves, not by whether the junction feels empty in the first month.

moved.what: The CJP 'Chappal protest' is set for today, Thursday 8 October, in Bengaluru, with Prakash Raj joining. A separate CJP protest against the CEC is announced for 10 October.
moved.so_what: The reports I fetched give no venue, so check the Traffic Police advisory before you leave. If you drive through the centre, leave early or take the metro, and expect the same again on Saturday.

moved.what: A rat triggered the transformer blast near the Amazon office, BESCOM says, and five people were injured in electrical equipment blasts in the city. Separately, an LPG cylinder blast killed a mother and her daughter in Nayandahalli.
moved.so_what: Stay clear of footpath transformer boxes when it rains, and report sparking or open ones to BESCOM. At home, check your cylinder hose and regulator for leaks and keep the kitchen ventilated before you light the stove.

moved.what: Bengaluru's unpaid traffic fines have crossed ₹2,048 crore.
moved.so_what: Check your own vehicle's pending challans on the official Karnataka Traffic Police portal, typing the address yourself. Never pay through a link sent by SMS.

moved.what: CMRS began a three-day safety inspection of the Pink Line elevated stretch on Bannerghatta Road, between Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere.
moved.so_what: Inspection comes before opening, but no opening date is in the reports. Don't plan a move or a commute change around it yet.

moved.what: The RBI raised rates, citing rising inflation and global risks.
moved.so_what: If your home or car loan floats, expect the EMI or tenure to rise at the next reset and ask your lender which one moves. Hold off on a large long-term borrowing decision this week.

moved.what: A report says the US administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorisation.
moved.so_what: If you or family are planning US study, treat the post-study work cost as unsettled. Wait for the final rule before paying any deposit that assumes it.
